title: Accuracy Weaver Harness with Hierarchical Golden Sets
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build an automated accuracy validation harness that composes hierarchical golden prompt sets, runs staged calibration profiles (FP8 and INT8), and evaluates contextual/regression metrics with pass/fail gating for rollouts.
background: We need a reproducible, multi-tiered acceptance system for quantized model rollouts. Current ad-hoc scripts and single-cohort golden sets are brittle for mixed workloads. This harness will enable layered golden families (sanity, functional, adversarial, customer-like) plus delta gating and signal aggregation so engineering and SRE can safely promote quantized builds to Dedicated and Private deployments.
goals: Design a hierarchical golden set schema (tier 0 sanity -> tier 1 functional -> tier 2 adversarial -> tier 3 customer cohorts)
Implement an orchestrator that runs calibration profiles for FP8 and INT8, records token-level and semantic metrics, and computes weighted pass/fail at each tier
Provide CI hooks and a staged gating workflow integrated with rollout config in Console
Ship dashboards and alerts for drift, majority-failure cohorts, and metric regressions
success_metrics: Automated acceptance check run time under 30m for baseline 20k utterance suite
False positive rejection rate below 2% vs. manual review on historical rollouts
Coverage of at least 4 distinct cohort tiers across model families
Integration with rollout pipeline enabling canary -> full rollout without manual gating for vetted models
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs deterministically with seedable randomness and produces an artifacts bundle (metrics CSV, diffs, sample failures)
Pass/fail gate computed as weighted aggregation across tiers and exposed via API and Console
FP8 and INT8 calibration runs supported via configuration with per-layer overrides
CI integration: PR comment with summary and link for any quantized model PRs that change runtime parameters
Dashboards show token-level latency and accuracy breakdown and cohort-level failure lists
plan: Phase 1: Schema and simple runner with tier0/1 golden sets and metric collector. Phase 2: Extend to adversarial/customer cohorts, add weighting and delta gating logic. Phase 3: CI hooks, Console integration, and alerting. Phase 4: Perf optimization and scale testing with 100k utterance suites.
milestones: 2026-02-12: Adversarial cohort ingestion and weighting engine
2026-03-01: Final validation on sample model family and handoff to release
tests: Deterministic replay: run same seed across environments and compare artifacts
Delta injection: synthetic perturbations to measure sensitivity of metric gates
Regression checks: run harness against previous release artifacts and assert no unexpected regressions
Stress: run 100k utterance suite on staging infra and measure runtime/telemetry
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit per-run metrics to metrics-prod.redwood: run.duration, run.failure_rate, tier0_failures, tier1_failures
Alert on run.duration > 60m and on tier2 failure_rate > 5%
Track long-term drift via weekly baseline comparison and create regression tickets automatically
rollout_plan: Start with internal model families on a dedicated test org
Enable canary gating for dedicated and private deployments using the harness pass/fail signal
If gate fails: automatic rollback to previous model variant and create incident ticket with failure artifacts
After 2 successful canary windows, allow automated full rollout
risks: Golden set curation bias may mask customer regressions; mitigation: include customer-like synthetic cohorts and rotate samples
Run time on large suites could be high; mitigation: progressive sampling and prefix caching during calibration
Overfitting to golden prompts; mitigation: adversarial generation and holdout cohorts
notes: Prefer implementation in Go for orchestrator consistency with runtime jobs; leverage existing runner infra (job-queue + k8s workers).
Keep artifacts small: store diffs and top-K failures rather than full raw responses when possible.
We should expose a library that evaluation engineers can import for bespoke cohort runs.
